title: sar-cose: minimal reference implementation of the Sovereign Acceptance Runtime (SAR)
description:
Reference implementation of the authorization path of the Sovereign Acceptance Runtime (SAR) described in the working paper Sovereign Acceptance Runtime: Verifiable Human Ratification and Evidentiary Audit Trails for Autonomous AI Agents under the EU AI Act (v1.1: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23270905; this software version accompanies v1.2).

Proposal and Ratification Statements are COSE_Sign1 objects (RFC 9052) over deterministic CBOR (RFC 8949 section 4.2.1), signed with Ed25519 (algorithm -19, RFC 9864). A fail-closed Execution Gate implements normative decision rules S1-S13 (SEMANTICS.md), including separation of roles and a single time rule under which the gate allows at an instant exactly when offline verification at that instant succeeds; it consumes each authorization before returning ALLOW (at most once) and can hand the executor exactly the digested payload bytes. A hash-chained SQLite store with signed checkpoints records every decision; an optional anchor retained outside the store detects rollback.

Includes a second implementation written by a separate AI-assistant instance from the paper and a fixed wire-format specification (with a reconstruction of its blind version), a 137-test suite (differential, property-based, cross-implementation, concurrency, crash-injection, rollback and revocation tests), 37 hand-written and 20 external audit mutants (all killed) and an automated mutation sweep (476/491 killed; the 15 survivors are argued decision-equivalent). Research prototype; SCITT Transparency Service integration (Receipts) is not implemented, and the guarantees hold only for actions routed through a trusted gate.
